title: Padding in Convolution
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Padding adds border values so convolution can preserve spatial size.
long: Add a border around image. Zero padding is common.

title: Stride in Convolution
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Stride is the step between successive kernel positions.
long: Larger stride means coarser output. It reduces resolution.

title: Receptive Field
subject: Computer Vision
statement: A unit receptive field is the input image region that can affect its activation.
long: Deeper units see more image. Grows with kernel size and stride.

title: Translation Equivariance of CNNs
subject: Computer Vision
statement: A CNN feature map shifts when the input shifts up to boundary and pooling effects.
long: Moving object moves features. Pooling trades exact equivariance for tolerance.

title: Pooling for Local Invariance
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Pooling reduces sensitivity to small shifts by discarding precise position.
long: Summarize region for tolerance. Heuristic not a theorem of invariance.

title: Edge Detection Kernels
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Finite difference kernels respond to intensity changes and act as simple edge detectors.
long: Gradients highlight edges. Sobel adds smoothing.

title: Hierarchical Feature Learning
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Early CNN layers learn simple features while deeper layers combine them into complex shapes.
long: Visual features build in stages. Empirical observation about trained nets.

title: ImageNet Benchmark
subject: Computer Vision
statement: ImageNet is a large labelled image dataset whose competition catalyzed deep learning.
short: A benchmark that changed the field.
long: A benchmark that changed the field. Historical fact about datasets.

title: Object Detection Task
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Object detection locates instances with bounding boxes and assigns class labels.
long: Find what and where. Combines classification and localization.

title: Intersection over Union
subject: Computer Vision
statement: IoU measures box overlap as intersection area divided by union area.
long: Overlap score for boxes. Equals one for perfect alignment.

title: Non Maximum Suppression
subject: Computer Vision
statement: NMS removes redundant detections by keeping highest scoring boxes and suppressing overlapping ones.
long: Deduplicate boxes. Greedy by score.

title: Region Based Detection
subject: Computer Vision
statement: R CNN style detectors first propose candidate regions then classify them.
long: Find candidates then recognize. Two stage trade offs historically.

title: Single Shot Detection
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Single shot detectors predict boxes and classes directly from feature maps in one pass.
long: Faster without proposals. YOLO style designs.

title: Semantic Segmentation
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Semantic segmentation assigns a class label to every pixel.
long: Label each pixel. Does not separate same class instances.

title: Instance Segmentation
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Instance segmentation detects objects and labels pixels of each separate instance.
long: Separate objects with masks. Combines detection and segmentation.

title: Fully Convolutional Networks
subject: Computer Vision
statement: FCNs replace classifier dense layers with convolutions for dense outputs.
long: Adapt classifiers to pixels. Upsampling restores resolution.

title: U Net Architecture
subject: Computer Vision
statement: U Net uses symmetric encoder decoder with skip connections for precise localization.
long: Contract then expand with shortcuts. Skips recover spatial detail.

title: Data Augmentation
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Augmenting images with label preserving transforms can improve generalization empirically.
long: Create extra examples. Heuristic encoding invariance priors.

title: Vision Transformer
subject: Computer Vision
statement: A vision transformer splits images into patches and applies a transformer to patch embeddings.
long: Images as patch sequences. Needs large pretraining.

title: Colour Space Conversion
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Colour spaces differ in separating luminance from chrominance which matters for tasks.
long: Choose representation for task. Lighting affects luminance.

title: Image Classification Task
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Image classification assigns one class label to an entire image.
long: One label per image. Simplest standard task.

title: Mixup Augmentation
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Mixup trains on convex combinations of images and labels encouraging smoother boundaries.
long: Blend pairs of examples. Empirical regularizer.

title: Translation Invariance in Recognition
subject: Computer Vision
statement: A classifier should label an object the same after it moves in the image.
long: Position should not change label. Architecture gives approximate invariance.

title: Convolutional Neural Network
subject: Computer Vision
statement: A convolutional neural network stacks convolutional nonlinear and pooling layers.
long: Deep hierarchical image model. Weights shared spatially.

title: Feature Map
subject: Computer Vision
statement: A feature map is the output grid produced by applying a filter across an image.
long: Filtered response grid. Each channel has one map.
